findings.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 — [P2 confidence 75] `query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(loaded, cacheKey, getRealm(), searchKey, cached, query);` copies every previously requested organization into one realm-and-mode cache object, so a realm that serves login pages for unbounded organization IDs grows and reserializes an unbounded aggregate on each new lookup until cache memory and cluster-transfer costs become a scalability cliff; although one entry per mode reduces cache-key count, that rebuttal fails because it merely moves the unbounded cardinality into each entry, and keying each organization separately deletes the copy-forward branch and isolates eviction and writes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural concern in the diff. Looking at lines 230-238, when a cache entry exists but the current organizationId search is not cached, the code creates a new IdentityProviderListQuery passing the existing query as the last parameter, which copies previous organization searches into the new entry. This pattern means each cache entry (one per FetchMode) accumulates all previously searched organizationIds. While this is a design choice rather than a bug (the code functions correctly), it's a legitimate scalability concern for realms with many organizations. The finding is grounded in specific code from the diff and raises a valid architectural issue about unbounded growth of cache entries.

Looking at the test code, `getForLogin(FetchMode.ORG_ONLY, orgaId)` is only called with a single organization ID throughout the test. The cache implementation in `getForLogin` uses `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` to store/retrieve cached results per organization.
